:::{#exm-moore-penrose-minimum-norm}
#### A rank-deficient least squares problem

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\vecf{b} = (2, 3)$.
By @exm-moore-penrose, $\matr{A}^+ = \matr{A}$, so $\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} = (2, 0)$ and $\matr{A}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} = (2, 0)$.

By @thm-moore-penrose-least-squares, $\vecf{x} = (x_1, x_2)$ is a least squares solution (@def-least-squares) [if and only if](proof-writing.qmd#def-iff)
$\matr{A}\vecf{x} = (x_1, 0) = (2, 0)$,
that is, $x_1 = 2$ with $x_2$ arbitrary.
Each of them leaves the same residual $\vecf{b} - \matr{A}\vecf{x} = (0, 3)$, of [norm](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-norm) $3$.

For these solutions,

$$
\norm{\vecf{x}}^2 = 4 + x_2^2
= \norm{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}^2 + \norm{\vecf{x} - \matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}^2,
$$

as @thm-moore-penrose-minimum-norm states.
The smallest is $4$, at $x_2 = 0$, which is $\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} = (2, 0)$.

:::
